## Audience Insight: Gen Z World Cup Behavior

### How Gen Z Watches
- **TikTok-first** — they get scores from TikTok, not ESPN
- **Creator-filtered** — they watch via their favorite creators, not broadcasters
- **Short-form native** — 6-15 second clips are native, not shortened
- **Emotion over stats** — they want FEELING, not scores
- **Fan identity content** — being a fan is part of their personality expression

### What Gen Z Shares
1. "When your team scores" reactions (identity)
2. "Bus was a party" moments (exclusivity/uniqueness)
3. Flag/stadium visuals (aesthetic/identity)
4. Bar/ home watching (belonging/community)
5. Behind-the-scenes fan journey (insider access)

**Our 5 scripts map directly to Gen Z sharing motivations.**

## Metadata Best Practices for World Cup Shorts

### YouTube Shorts Specifics
- **Upload as Shorts** (not regular video) — YouTube surfaces Shorts separately
- **Add #Shorts to title** — algorithmic signal
- **9:16 aspect ratio mandatory** — enforced by YouTube
- **First 3 seconds are everything** — hook before skip
- **End screen CTA:** "Follow for more World Cup moments ⚽"

### TikTok Specifics
- **Post at 6pm local time** — peak sports content consumption
- **Use trending sounds** when applicable (FIFA has official partnerships)
- **Duet-friendly hooks** — make first frame reactable
- **Engage in comments** — reply to every comment in first hour (algorithm boost)
